newsitem.title: CHINA: Old reservoirs plague China's fight against floods.
newsitem.headline: Old reservoirs plague China's fight against floods.

text.p: Crumbling water conservancy facilities, land reclamation and flagging investment are exacerbating China's annual battle against floods, the Economic Information Daily said on Wednesday.
About two-fifths of small reservoirs and one-fourth of medium-sized and large reservoirs across China needed repairs, the newspaper said.
"No doubt it is like hanging a sharp dagger over the heads of people living in downstream areas" near crumbling reservoirs, it said.
"Once a dam collapses, the accident will create a deadly disaster," the newspaper said.
The quality of water conservancy facilities in 420 cities across China was below the national level, it said. About 70 cities had no water conservancy facilities at all.

Despite repeated directives from the central government, many local governments had been reluctant to spend money on water conservancy facilities because such investments did not generate revenue, the newspaper said.
Pledges to boost investment in water conservancy were restricted to documents and slogans, it said.
As a result, rivers threatened to burst their banks at more and more places, it said. The mighty Yangtze river threatened to burst its banks in 2,800 places in floods this year.
Reclamation of land was also threatening anti-flood work, the newspaper said. About 1.3 million hectares (3.2 million acres) of land has been reclaimed in the past 40 years.
The area of Dongting lake in central China had been reduced by one third, it said. Rainfall this year in the area was not a record but the water level of the lake hit a record.
"All these are the result of our violating the pattern of nature," the newspaper said.

Summer floods that ravaged much of southern and northeastern China this year have caused a record 220 billion yuan ($26.5 billion) in damage, Sun Zhongzu, spokesman for the Ministry of Water Resources, was quoted as saying last week.

The losses were triple those of devastating floods in 1991 that caused 80 billion yuan ($9.6 billion) in damage, Sun said. Three months of flooding this year killed at least 2,700 people, injured more than 32,200 and left hundreds of thousands homeless, according to the latest official figures.
